title: Microcontroller Architecture
subtitle: CPU, memory, registers, interrupts, and peripherals

content.text: A microcontroller contains a CPU, program flash (non-volatile), data SRAM (volatile), timers, ADC, and digital I/O all on one chip.

content.code:
ATmega328P (Arduino Uno) architecture:
  CPU:    8-bit AVR @ 16 MHz
  Flash:  32 KB (stores your program)
  SRAM:   2 KB  (runtime data — use carefully!)
  EEPROM: 1 KB  (persistent small data)
  Timers: 3 (Timer0/1/2)
  ADC:    10-bit, 6 channels
  UART, SPI, I2C built in

content.definition: Analog-to-Digital Converter: reads an analog voltage (0-5V) and converts it to a digital number (0-1023 for 10-bit).
A signal that pauses the main program to handle an urgent event (button press, timer tick, data received).

content.text: SRAM is precious on Arduino. Store large constant data in flash with PROGMEM; prefer local variables over global.

questions.question: Where is a running Arduino program stored?
questions.explanation: Program code is stored in flash (non-volatile). SRAM holds runtime variables and disappears when power is lost.

faq.q: What happens when SRAM runs out?
faq.a: Stack and heap collide, causing random crashes or data corruption. This is a common Arduino bug. Monitor free SRAM with freeMemory().
